title: רב יעקב בר (רב) אידי

paragraphs: Rav Yaakov bar (Rav) Idi, a student-colleague of R. Yoḥanan, who said, 'Like ben Idi, our colleague,' Yevamot (96, end of side b). This proof is not conclusive: in the phrase 'ben Idi, our colleague,' perhaps 'our colleague' refers to Idi. Yet we find that R. Yaakov learned from R. Yehoshua ben Levi, as did R. Yoḥanan; thus R. Yaakov was both R. Yoḥanan's colleague and his student. Admittedly one cannot interpret 'our colleague' as referring to Idi, who was a 'student of the study house for one day' before R. Yoḥanan (see his entry). However, Ein Yaakov's reading is that Idi son of R. Yaakov was the 'student of the study house for one day'; if so, Idi, his paternal grandfather, was R. Yoḥanan's colleague. I think there is another proof that he was a student-colleague: in the chapter Ellu Terefot (57b), 'R. Yoḥanan said,' etc.; R. Yaakov bar Idi said, 'Had R. Yoḥanan been in the place where the colleagues ruled permissively, he would not have fluttered.' Rashi explains: 'He would not have been able to move a wing and object'—for he would not have spoken this way about his teacher. He said, 'R. Yoḥanan said,' Eruvin (46b). R. Abba, his son. They used to call his father 'student of the study house for one day' (according to Ein Yaakov's reading, [this refers] to Rav Idi, R. Yaakov's father). See below, nearby, another R. Yaakov bar Idi, and consider which seems preferable to you. R. Abba bar Pappa. He said, 'R. Oshaya said,' Berakhot (29b). And Rav Aḥ bar Ḥanina. He and Rav Ila were sitting; Shemuel bar Ba passed, and they rose before him. He said to them, 'I have two claims against you: first, I am not old; and second, Torah does not stand before its son,' Jerusalem Talmud, Bikkurim, last chapter, halakhah 3. R. Zeira said to R. Abba bar Pappa: 'Go to the Ladder of Tyre, to R. Yaakov bar Idi, and ask him whether he heard it from R. Yoḥanan (his teacher),' Bava Metzia (43b). He said, 'R. Yehoshua ben Levi said,' etc. R. Zeira said to R. Yaakov bar Idi: 'Did you hear this explicitly from R. Yehoshua ben Levi, or [infer it] by implication?' Eruvin (46a). In the chapter HaBa Al Yevimto (60, end of side b): R. Yaakov bar Idi said: R. Yehoshua ben Levi said. R. Zeira said to R. Yaakov bar Idi: 'Did you hear this explicitly from R. Yehoshua ben Levi?' R. Zeira did not call him 'my teacher'; he simply addressed him as 'you.' In the first chapter of Ḥullin (5b), however, R. Zeira said to R. Yaakov bar Idi, 'Perhaps my teacher did not hear ...' (see his entry). R. Zerikan, in his name. Ḥama, the father of R. Oshaya (see below). He said, 'R. Ḥanina said,' Berakhot (44a). R. Ḥanan said: R. Yaakov bar Idi said: R. Yehoshua ben Levi said, Ḥullin (5b). R. Yehoshua ben Levi appears to have been his teacher, for he said, 'R. Yehoshua ben Levi said,' in the chapter Asarah Yuḥasin (75b), Gittin (86b), and the Jerusalem Talmud at the end of Rosh HaShanah and the end of Sotah. In his neighborhood was an old man who went out in a sedan chair [גלודקי; provisional reading], and they asked R. Yehoshua ben Levi, Beitzah (25b). R. Yoḥanan, his teacher, in whose name he spoke (see above). In R. Yonatan's name, Jerusalem Talmud, end of Bikkurim and chapter Bammeh Tomin, halakhah 2. R. Yaakov bar bat Yaakov. In the name of Yitzḥak Rabba, Jerusalem Talmud, chapter Ein Omedin, mishnah 2. Rav Naḥman (see above). R. Naḥman said to Ḥama bar Adda, the messenger of Zion: 'When you go up, make a detour by the Ladder of Tyre, go to R. Yaakov bar Idi, and ask him.' Before the messenger arrived, R. Yaakov bar Idi died, Beitzah (25b). He and Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak were administrators and gave [support] to R. Ḥama, R. Oshaya's father (see his entry). In R. Simai's name, Ma'aser Sheni, chapter 4, halakhah 7 as printed (the corresponding passage is 4:2:3). R. Pedat, in his name. Ravin, in his name (see below, nearby). In the name of R. Shimon ben Lakish, Kilayim, chapter 4, halakhah 3 as printed (a matching chain occurs at 6:3:2). When Ravin came: R. Yaakov bar Idi said: R. Shimon Ḥasida said, at the end of Rosh HaShanah. In R. Shimon Ḥasida's name, Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot, chapter 4, mishnah 6. He disagrees with R. Shemuel bar Naḥmani in the chapter HaRo'eh (62b).
